hydration.title: Hydration Protocol
hydration.description: Optimal fluid intake is the foundation of athletic performance and core body temperature regulation.
guidelines: Daily Base: 30–40 ml per kg of body weight.
Pre-Training: 5–7 ml/kg of water 4 hours before exercise.
During Training: 150–250 ml every 15–20 mins (add electrolytes for sessions >60 mins).
Post-Training: 1.25–1.5L of fluid for every 1kg of weight lost.
tips: Always carry a reusable water bottle.
Add a pinch of sea salt or electrolytes to water during high-intensity sessions.
Drink consistently, don't wait until you feel thirsty.

pre_training.title: Pre-Training Nutrition
pre_training.description: Fueling your muscles with the right energy sources to sustain high-intensity efforts.
what_to_eat: Include a small amount of lean Protein.
Keep Fats and Fiber low to avoid stomach discomfort.
pre_training.timing: Aim to eat 30–90 minutes before your session begins.
examples: Banana with a small amount of peanut butter
A small bowl of oats with berries
Two slices of white toast with honey
Low-fat yogurt with a handful of granola

post_training.title: Post-Training Recovery
post_training.description: Repair muscle tissue and replenish glycogen stores immediately after exertion.
post_training.protein: 20–30g of high-quality protein (Whey, Chicken, Greek Yogurt).
post_training.carbs: 0.8–1.2g/kg of carbohydrates to refill energy stores.
examples: Grilled chicken breast with white rice and steamed greens
Whey protein shake with a medium banana
Chocolate milk (Excellent 3:1 Carb to Protein ratio)
Greek yogurt with honey and sliced almonds

anti_inflammatory.title: Anti-Inflammatory Nutrition
anti_inflammatory.description: Natural compounds that help dampen systemic inflammation and accelerate tissue repair.
foods: Omega-3s: Fatty fish (Salmon, Mackerel), Walnuts, Chia Seeds.
Fruits: Blueberries, Tart Cherries, Strawberries, Oranges.
anti_inflammatory.benefits: These foods help reduce muscle soreness (DOMS), protect joints, and support the immune system during heavy training cycles.

performance_tips.detail: Dehydration of just 2% can significantly impair cognitive function and physical power.
High-sugar/high-fat foods cause energy crashes and digestive sluggishness.
Ensure every main meal has a quality protein source, complex carbs, and healthy fats.
Consistent post-run fueling reduces the risk of Overreaching and bone stress injuries.
